params.body:
## What was wrong

In the own stock list, on screens narrower than 1550px, the photo of a row showed as a flat strip: the top of the photo, 60px wide and about 28px high.

The rule for that width set the thumbnail frame to `width: 60px; height: auto`. The frame holds an absolutely positioned photo over a placeholder, so `auto` made the frame as high as the placeholder icon (26px) and not as high as a photo. The same rule also set `height: auto` on the photo itself, which overruled the `height: 100%` that makes it fill its frame.

## What changes

- The frame gets a photo's proportions below 1550px: 66 by 44px (it is 74 by 50px above that width, unchanged).
- The `height: auto` no longer applies to the photo inside a frame (`.ui-photo-img`), so the photo fills the frame and is cropped by `object-fit: cover` as it is on wide screens.

Two lines in `resources/css/refresh.css`; the file does not grow. Rows become about 16px higher on those screens, which is the height the photo needs.

## Not checked

Not rendered locally with real photos (the local demo data has none); the same frame size was checked on a local branch with the placeholder. CI is the judge for the stylesheet tests.
params.title: The row thumbnail keeps a photo's height below 1550px
